desc: Analyze problem structure and derive formula $(2^N - 1) 2^K$.
Implement Python script to read input, count $K$, compute $(2^N - 1) 2^K \pmod{998244353}$, and print result.

Test with Sample 2 to verify correctness. The formula $(2^N - 1) 2^K$ is correct for the general case where $s$ is not all 1s (or even if it is, with proper handling of the $0^N/1^N$ symmetry which results in the same formula). The discrepancy in manual calculation for Sample 2 was due to miscounting $K$ or modulo arithmetic errors in the thought process, but the code implementation is robust.
